News.title: Teacher, 37, ‘who had sex with student after flirty Instagram chats’ caught when boy lied to parents about ‘girlfriend’
News.content:
SICK TRYSTS Teacher, 37, ‘who had sex with student after flirty Instagram chats’ caught when boy lied to parents about ‘girlfriend’

A MATH teacher has been busted in the midst of an alleged tryst with a student after the boy revealed the identity of his “secret” girlfriend, according to authorities.

Kirsten Rose, 37, was arrested on Friday for allegedly having sex with one of her students.





The Florida educator was accused of beginning to chat with the young boy outside class on social media five months ago, according to court documents.

Police allege the pair continued to speak on Instagram into the new year, before they allegedly had sex in February and March.

The boy’s parents first became suspicious after he returned home late from work one evening in March.

After noticing his location appear at an unfamiliar address, his parents confronted him.



Caught in the late night lie, the student claimed to have been at his “girlfriend’s” house.

At first, he did not name Rose.

But after his parents continued to question him, the alleged illicit tryst between the pair was exposed.

The boy allegedly admitted he had been in a relationship with his teacher.



Rose had been working at the Cocoa Beach Jr/Sr High School at the time of the alleged offending.

Police revealed they opened an investigation into the vile allegations immediately after the parents made an initial report.

Investigators said the evidence revealed the student and Rose allegedly began communicating outside of school through Instagram in November last year.

A spokesperson from the Brevard County Sheriff’s Office said the school had taken “immediate action” and placed Rose on “administrative leave”.

The school also released a statement, saying it was “cooperating fully with law enforcement”.



“We are deeply troubled by these allegations,” the statement read.

“The District remains committed to providing a safe and supportive learning environment for all students.”

On Friday Rose was charged with five counts of unlawful sexual activity with a minor, following a police probe.

She is being held without bond at the Brevard County Jail.

Her arraignment is set for May 5.



The investigation into the alleged illicit relationship remains ongoing, with police searching for possible additional alleged victims, Fox35 reported.

News.title: Illegal migrant WINS latest bid to stay in UK because he once had a fling with Brazilian drug cartel gangster’s wife
News.content:
FLING FURY Illegal migrant WINS latest bid to stay in UK because he once had a fling with Brazilian drug cartel gangster’s wife

AN ILLEGAL migrant has won his latest bid to remain in the UK because he once had a fling with the ex-wife of a cartel member.

The man argued that if he were deported back to Brazil he would face death at the hands of the feared Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC).



PCC is Brazil‘s largest organised crime group and is known worldwide for its class A drug trade, supplying Europe with a lot of its cocaine.

Primeiro Comando da Capital – which translates to First Capital Command – is said to control a drug trade worth a billion dollars.



It has a reputation for being violent, with murder, inhumane treatment and torture being commonplace in the organised crime group’s activities.

The Brazilian migrant argued that if the PCC gangster found out he had been having a relationship with his wife, his life would be put in danger.

At the British asylum court, the migrant was granted anonymity and won an appeal to have his immigration case heard again.

He came to the UK in January 2023 as a visitor before making two applications to remain and being arrested as an overstayer in 2024.



His attempt to claim asylum was refused and it was found he would have no problem reintegrating into Brazil.

He had spent most of his life in the South American country, spoke the language, and had family support available.

Now, he has won an appeal after an immigration judge found that there had been errors in the First-Tier Tribunal judgment.

The migrant – anonymised as “DL” – said he feared the PCC because of his relationship with a woman who is understood to be the ex-wife of a PCC member.



The woman, referred to as C, and the ex-husband, referred to as S, remain anonymous for legal reasons.

DL also said that he owed an outstanding debt to a moneylender, who he feared would be violent to him.

The migrant added that he had been diagnosed with anxiety, depression, and post‑traumatic stress disorder.

He argued his mental health would make it difficult for him to reintegrate if he were forced to return to Brazil.

Deputy Upper Tribunal Judge Harbinder Athwal ruled there had been errors in law made by a previous ruling because it had not believed the migrant’s evidence that the ex-husband was part of the PCC.



A new hearing will now take place to determine whether DL should be granted asylum or be deported.

Judge Athwal said that there had been too much weight placed on an “inconsistency” in evidence from the migrant when he said that the way he knew the ex-husband was part of the PCC was through his brother being told.

In an asylum letter, the migrant had said that his family told him that S was a member of PCC but did not mention his brother.

Judge Athwal said: “In reaching her conclusion, the Judge placed weight on a material factual error, namely her finding that [DL] had given inconsistent accounts of how he knew that S was associated with PCC.

“That finding was itself inconsistent with her earlier conclusion that [DL’s] account was consistent with the expert evidence.



“The Judge erred by firstly treating this aspect of the evidence as inconsistent; and secondly in making inconsistent findings about this evidence.

“In consequence, the Judge did not correctly evaluate the actual evidence in the round.

“I therefore find that the Judge made a material error of law.

“I am therefore satisfied that these errors of law materially impacted the Judge’s decision and that this should be set aside.

“It follows that the [DL] has established that the Judge’s decision is infected by an error on a point of law.”

News.title: ‘Petrified’ dual-national Brit stranded in Spain because of new £589 passport rule says ‘the government have failed’
News.content:
BORDER HELL ‘Petrified’ dual-national Brit stranded in Spain because of new £589 passport rule says ‘the government have failed’

A YOUNG woman born and bred in England has been denied entry into the UK and left stranded in Spain under a bizarre new passport rule.

Natasha Cochrane De La Rosa, 26, has been blocked from entering the country despite being a dual national and flashing officials her British birth certificate.





The young Brit tried to board a plane back to England from a holiday trip to Amsterdam on April 2 when the airline determined that she did not have the correct documents to return.

New immigration rules launched by the government in February 2025 state that dual British nationals must have a British passport or a £539 Certificate of Entitlement to enter England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

Natasha had no idea about the new rule changes and breezed through check in, security and passport control until she was stopped just before boarding her plane back home.

Not able to return home, she spent a terrifying night in a Dutch airport before flying the next day to stay with family friends in Spain, where she remains now.



She told the Daily Mail that her attempts to persuade the Home Office to let her back in to the UK have been a “nightmare”.

“It’s terrifying and I’m petrified,” she said, not knowing when she can come home and fearing the loss of her job as a client success manager in London.

“I was born in Islington, I have paid taxes, I have voted” she added.

“I feel abandoned by my own country. A system that can leave a British-born person stranded abroad, unable to return home without entering a maze of contradictory guidance and delays, is a system that deserves urgent scrutiny”.



Natasha was born to a British father and a Spanish mother in 1999, during a time when the law said that any child born in the UK with a British parent is a British citizen.

Dual nationals are barred from applying for the £10 Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) which can be purchased by foreign nationals to enter the country.

The client success manager has applied for a British passport, a process which may leave her stranded abroad for a further three to six weeks.

In a worrying twist however there is a chance that her passport application will be rejected because her parents were not married at the time of her birth.

“If I didn’t have family in Spain, they would have left me effectively homeless in Amsterdam”, she said. “Its absolutely despicable”.



A government spokesperson said: “Public information advising dual nationals to carry the correct documentation has been available since October 2024 and a substantive communications campaign about the introduction of ETA has been running since 2023”.

They said the changes are in line with controls in the United States, Canada and Australia.

What are the new border rules for dual nationals? Dual nationals can no longer enter Britain on their foreign passports - unless they shell out for a pricey £539 Certificate of Entitlement. According to guidance which came into force on February 25, the Home Office demands that all British citizens entering the UK must have a British passport or a Certificate of Entitlement. British birth certificates, driving licenses, citizenship certificates and HMRC documents are not valid for entry into the UK. The new rules mimic immigration controls in Australia, Canada and the US.

It comes as queasy holidaymers are “left vomiting” in hour long queues at EU borders.

Desperate travellers were stricken by a Milanese heatwave as they queued for up to three hours in Italy to board a plane back to the UK.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Unfortunately, one EasyJet plane flying from Milan to Manchester took off without 100 passengers as the heat-stricken holidaymakers struggled to get past new borders requiring fingerprint scanning.



The massive queues are due to EU border rule changes which require all British nationals to scan their fingerprints before boarding.

News.title: ‘Put my dog & its PUPPIES down’, says dad whose daughter, 19, was mauled to death by family pet
News.content:
THE heartbroken dad of a teenage girl mauled to death by her “loving” family dog has begged police to destroy it – as well as her two puppies.

Jack Biscoe found his daughter Jamie-Lea, 19, dead at home on Friday evening.





She had been attacked by pet Shy and was slumped over on the floor with a bite wound to her neck.

Emergency services were called to the family home in the village of Leaden Roding near Dunmow, Essex, at 10.45pm.

But despite the best efforts of medical teams, the teen was sadly pronounced dead at the scene.



Dad-of-one Jack, 37, told The Sun he pleaded with cops who seized the female blue-merle Lurcher-cross to put her to sleep immediately.

He said: “I just said to them ‘please just put her down’.

“I don’t want to see her ever again… I just don’t think that dog should live anymore.”

Police confirmed on Sunday that tests are underway to formally establish Shy’s breed.



They are also understood to be conducting forensic examinations to prove she carried out the fatal attack.

Jack said: “We know that she did. She was the one that was covered in blood and she attacked me.”

His other dogs Bella and Mouse – Shy’s 18-month-old pups – are not thought to have been involved in the attack which killed Jamie-Lea.

But horse trainer Jack is also calling for them to be destroyed.

He said: “Those dogs have seen too much. They need to be put down in my opinion. I don’t want them to live in this world now.



“Even though the youngsters didn’t do anything, they’ve seen too much and I don’t think they could ever be placed with a family again…

“They could never possibly be rehomed after that situation. I think the best thing for them would be to put them to sleep.”

Jack, who bought Shy as a puppy at seven weeks old, said there had been no indication the family dog was dangerous.

He told how the pet had no history of biting or ­aggressive behaviour and described her as the “softest dog”.



While trying to revive his daughter, who had collapsed on the floor between his bed and bedside table, Jack was also attacked by Shy.

She bit off part of his ear, which will require reconstructive surgery, and left puncture wounds in his arms.

The devasted dad added: “My daughter was not killed by an XL Bully, she was killed by a genuine family dog.

“I thought I could trust that dog with my life and it took my daughter’s life. She was my daughter’s best friend and she still killed her.

“I lost my entire life on Friday when my daughter was murdered by another member of my family.



“Witnessing the horror and destruction it has caused me, it’s not worth it. Treat them as dogs, give them their beds, be careful.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Jack was arrested on suspicion of being in charge of a dog dangerously out of control and causing injury resulting in death.

He was released on bail on ­Saturday night.

News.title: Dad, 48, took own life after losing all his teeth following botched dental treatment in Turkey
News.content:
OP TRAGEDY Dad, 48, took own life after losing all his teeth following botched dental treatment in Turkey

A DAD took his own life after losing all his teeth following botched dental treatment in Turkey, an inquest heard.

Pawel Bukowski, 48, had suffered for years with periodontal disease, a chronic inflammatory condition that can lead to tooth and bone loss.





The forklift driver decided to pay to have his teeth taken out and later replaced by implants at a cut-price private clinic in Turkey.

Norfolk Coroner’s Court heard how Pawel expected to be fitted with temporary dentures in January last year before getting permanent implants.

But he was sent home without any dentures after his teeth were removed and was told he would have to wait six months for his new implants.

Pawel began drinking heavily and battled with depression after his mental health declined.

His wife Daria Bukowska told the inquest: “He lost all hope that things could improve.

“Despite all our efforts to support him, we were ultimately unable to save him.”

The court heard Polish-born Pawel had lived in the UK for two decades had always taken pride in himself but his confidence was shattered by the loss of his teeth.

Describing his dental treatment, Daria said: “Unfortunately, after removing all of his teeth, the clinic told him they could not proceed further.



“They sent him home without any teeth and told him to return in six months. This was emotionally devastating for him.

“He was deeply broken emotionally, losing his teeth had destroyed his self-confidence and sense of hope. Despite our constant support, from me and his daughters, he was slipping away from us.”

Daria said Pawel’s mental health “deteriorated rapidly” – leading to emergency services being called on the evening of April 24 last year.

The dad-of-three was referred to the mental health liaison team where a practitioner concluded he was “hopeless with a strong suicidal ideation”, it was said.

But it was decided he did not require psychiatric admission at that time due to “sufficient protective factors” and “some evidence of future planning”.



Pawel was instead referred to the crisis team, with the expectation that he could be admitted if necessary.

The court heard he was sent home with his family, who were given safety advice and a small supply of medication for him.

But the following day, a nurse was unable to prescribe further medication due to concerns over his “heavy” drinking.

A psychiatrist visited Pawel at his home on April 28 – three hours later than arranged due to staff sickness – and tragically found him dead.

Daria criticised her husband’s care, saying the severity of his problems had been “overlooked at every chance”.



She said in a statement to the court: “He was never given anything to help with the withdrawal symptoms [of alcohol].

“He was not given the medication he needed to keep him going for a few days. Workers did not show up, did not call us back, and finally were late.

“The accumulation of these things, the lack of communication, ultimately lead to where we are today.

“We as a family were not supported whatsoever with signs to look out for suicide, how to manage his withdrawal, how to support him.

“We trusted the expertise of workers to help us and him to get through this. Pawel may be just another case to people. To us, he was our world. We loved him deeply, and now we have to live through our worst nightmare.



“Pawel was failed at crucial points. I hope that this is never repeated, that other families get to keep their dads, husbands, brothers and sons. Pawel deserved better.”

How to get help EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. If you, or anyone you know, needs help dealing with mental health problems, the following organisations provide support: CALM, www.thecalmzone.net, 0800 585 858

Heads Together,www.headstogether.org.uk

HUMEN www.wearehumen.org

Mind, www.mind.org.uk, 0300 123 3393

Papyrus, www.papyrus-uk.org, 0800 068 41 41

Samaritans,www.samaritans.org, 116 123

Ruling a conclusion of suicide, Norfolk Area coroner Johanna Thompson said the failed dental treatment had a profound impact on Pawel’s wellbeing.

She also Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust carried out an investigation following his death.

The coroner added: “An investigation following his death did identify several lessons learnt.

It is clear there were factors which impacted upon the care provided to Pawel.



“He’d not been admitted when he presented to hospital with concerning suicidal ideation, and this may have been a missed opportunity for him to receive more intensive intervention than that which occurred.”

The Sun Online has contacted Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust.

If you are affected by any of the issues raised in this article, please call the Samaritans for free on 116123.

News.title: Horror viral doorbell vid shows creep kicking stranger’s door & screaming ‘where’s your daughter’…before getting inside
News.content:
THIS is the frightening moment a sicko demands to be let inside a stranger’s home after asking “where’s your daughter”.

The horrifying incident has shocked locals in the quiet Fairfield, California, neighbourhood after footage of the creep breaking into the home went viral online.





The conversation begins innocently, as a man in a long black coat, flip flops and glasses asks the owner to “please” open the door.

The man, later identified by authorities as Jason Nichols, 30, explains: “I just want to make sure everything is OK. I just figured I would check on something.”

A woman with her child are inside the house at the time but she is too terrified to open the door.

Her husband, who isn’t at home, tries to persuade Nichols to go away via the doorcam microphone.

The owner replies: “I don’t know what you want man, get out of my house.”

That reply infuriates Nichols, who kicked the front door and started screaming in fury.

“Open this f***ing door. Where is your daughter man? Who’s in there with you. Open the door or I’m breaking it f***ing down. Is everybody in this house OK?” he rages.



The homeowner can be heard begging him to leave.

Nichols then asks in a menacing tone: “Open the door. This is my neighbourhood. Now…. Or I’ll f***ing end you. Do you understand me?”

He then aggressively rips off the doorbell while pounding the door.

Nichols then reportedly found a way inside the home by slipping through a sliding glass door.

Another security camera inside the house caught Nichols striding through the house, opening cupboards and doors looking for the wife and child.



The homeowner raced back to his home armed with a shovel to protect his wife and child.

He and Nichols reportedly exchanged blows causing each other head injuries, police said.

Fairfield police arrived just minutes later and found Nichols outside.



He was taken to a nearby hospital on April 7 before being booked into jail on multiple felony charges tied to the brazen break-in attempt.

Despite the terrifying ordeal, the woman and child inside the home were not physically harmed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Nichols had his bail set at $35,000, and is due in court on Tuesday afternoon.

Police praised “the actions of the homeowner, who worked to protect his family while officers were responding to the scene.”

News.title: Chilling moment Russians blow up their OWN wounded soldiers – not realising they were PoWs sent by Ukraine to test truce
News.content:
HOMICIDAL Russian troops were duped into blowing up their own wounded soldiers – not realising they were prisoners of war sent by Ukraine to test the Easter truce.

Chilling footage shows deadly FPV drones swooping in on three plainly injured fighters in a cold-blooded attack.





Murderous drone pilots appeared to believe the unarmed trio were Ukrainian troops, brazenly carrying out the strikes in the midst of Vladimir Putin’s holiday ceasefire.

One of the men can be seen hobbling on crutches, while another desperately waves a white flag – yet all three come cruelly under attack.

But Kyiv‘s forces had sent out three Russian prisoners of war dressed in “neutral uniforms”, suspecting Putin’s bloodthirsty troops would exploit their own truce to strike.

The Ukrainian 24th Separate Mechanised Brigade said it was “checking the enemy’s compliance with the ceasefire promises” near Chasiv Yar in the fiercely contested Donetsk region.

Their fears proved deadly and the three Russian men – named as Private A.A. Choshev, Junior Sergeant A.V. Zagrebin and Senior Sergeant S.A. Zhuravlev – were killed by their own.

“The enemy is not keeping its own promises of a ceasefire and is killing its own Russian soldiers,” the brigade said.

A video released by the unit adds: “Wounded soldiers leave their positions unarmed.



“The enemy identifies the evacuation team and attacks with FPV drones.

“The evacuation was unsuccessful. All soldiers were killed.

“The enemy violates the ceasefire again.”

The Ukrainians admitted that they deliberately sent the POWs out as a test.

They said the move was aimed at allowing them to “safely evacuate the personnel of its units”, with commanders deciding to dress the captured soldiers in neutral uniforms.



The tactic could raise questions under the rules of war and is likely to be probed.

But the incident also lays bare what Kyiv says is Russia’s blatant disregard for a truce personally ordered by Putin.

Ukraine claims there were 2,299 violations of the ceasefire in just the first 15 hours of the planned 32-hour pause.



These included 28 assault operations, 479 shelling incidents, 747 kamikaze drone attacks and 1,045 FPV drone strikes.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky had promised on Saturday to respect the ceasefire.

He described it as an opportunity to build on peace initiatives – but warned there would be a swift military response to any violations.

Previous ceasefire attempts over Easter throughout the grueling four-year war have had little impact – with Putin consistently violating the terms.

Hours before the ceasefire was due to begin, another drone onslaught from the Russian dictator killed at least two people in Odesa.



It comes after Ukraine claimed Putin’s war funds were running out – as Russia tried to hint that a peace deal was “on the horizon”.

Ukraine’s top negotiator Lt-Gen Kyrylo Budanov, 40, said Russia is shifting its stance.

He told Bloomberg: “They all understand the war needs to end. That’s why they are negotiating.



“I don’t think it will be long.”

Budanov also said Russia was moving to an endgame because the “trillions” it has spent on the conflict was taking its toll.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Russia‘s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 has seen the country’s defence costs skyrocket, hitting £144billion in 2025.

It has left the country on the verge of an economic breakdown as the war drags on into its fifth year, as the desperate Kremlin ploughs millions into the conflict.

News.title: Man, 27, charged with murder after student stabbed to death at UK beauty spot tells court ‘you’ve got the wrong man’
News.content:
BLADE HORROR Man, 27, charged with murder after student stabbed to death at UK beauty spot tells court ‘you’ve got the wrong man’

A MAN charged with murdering a student who was stabbed to death at a UK beauty spot has appeared in court.

Tragic filmmaker Finbar Sullivan, 21, was killed in Primrose Hill, North London, last Tuesday.





Oliuwadamilola Ogunyankinnu today appeared at Stratford Magistrates’ Court charged with murder.

The 27-year-old, of Enfield, North London, told the court: “I didn’t kill anybody, I didn’t stab anybody, they’ve got the wrong person.”

He was remanded into custody to next appear at the Old Bailey on Wednesday.

A 25-year-old man arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender had been released with no further action, police said.

The horror unfolded on Tuesday evening at around 6.30pm at the viewpoint, which was “very busy” due to the holidays and sunny weather.

Despite the efforts of paramedics, Finbar was tragically pronounced dead at the scene.

Another man, believed to be in his 20s, was located nearby and taken to hospital for non-life threatening injuries.



Finbar’s dad Christopher Sullivan, 65, previously told the Daily Mail his son had gone to the area to use a new camera he received for his birthday.

He said his son had ambitions to follow in the footsteps of his grandfather, cameraman Michael Seresin, who worked on Harry Potter And The Prisoner Of Azkaban and Rambo III.

Christopher said: “This is the worst tragedy I could ever imagine.

“He’s my only son… I had him when I was 45. He can never be replaced.”

News.title: 'I've eaten dinner with King Charles and he has a very strict rule staff must follow'
News.content:
'I've eaten dinner with King Charles and he has a very strict rule staff must follow'

Queen Camilla's son has shared what it's like to dine with The King, and revealed the one rule he has for diners when it comes to a royal meal - as well as 'competing' with Camilla

View 3 Images Charles always sticks to this eating rule (Image: Getty Images)

When it comes to a royal banquet, King Charles has very strict rules for guests.

‌



With lavish tablescapes and lashings of food, it's hard to imagine the royals getting through all of the grub that's served to them. But according to Queen Camila's son, the King is a passionate advocate for recycling who "appalls waste".

‌



Food critic and author Tom Parker Bowles revealed that his stepfather Charles refuses to let anything be discarded after mealtimes, insisting that leftovers can be transformed into other dishes with all packaging properly recycled.

‌



Tom, 49, said: "There is no waste, everything is recycled, everything is used from the table. If anything is leftover from the dinner, that will be made into something else or appear the next day. Nothing's allowed to be thrown out."

Queen Mary's father dies after suffering years of health problems aged 84 READ MORE :

View 3 Images Camilla with son Tom Parker Bowles, who lifted the lid on his stepfather (Image: Dave Benett/Getty Images)

The King has long championed sustainability – The Coronation Food Project, coordinated by his charitable fund and launched last year, aims to tackle food waste while supporting those living in "food insecurity". Parker Bowles added: "It's not the King just paying lip service, he practices what he preaches."

‌



As both the King's stepson and godson, he says food sustainability is a topic he "can relate to" when speaking with the monarch. "He really is a food hero. To talk to him about the strange varieties of plums or pears or anything else is endlessly fascinating", he added.

His book, Cooking and the Crown, chronicles the history of cuisine within the royal household - spanning from Queen Victoria's reign commencing in 1837 and Edward VII at the dawn of the last century, right through to Charles and Camilla. "They can certainly eat that family!" joked the author - a familiar face as a judge on BBC One's MasterChef.

In Queen Victoria's era, lunch and dinner would stretch to between 10 and 12 courses. "They didn't have to eat it all but there was just a huge amount of food and they did eat a lot more than we do now."

‌



The writer also says that both Charles and Camilla are "deeply competitive" when it comes to foraging for mushrooms during their time at Balmoral.

View 3 Images Camilla, now-Queen Consort, and son Tom Parker Bowles, in 2014 (Image: Getty Images for Fortnum & Mason)

He revealed: "They're both very keen mycologists, and both know their mushrooms very, very well. This time of year, depending on rain, there's ceps and chanterelles... I go with my mother and there's a lot of fantastic mushrooming in Scotland. It's a shared pleasure."

Article continues below

Parker Bowles notes that the King and Queen are considerably less wasteful, opting for more modest portions than earlier generations of royals. Throughout the winter months, Camilla enjoys a daily bowl of porridge - a recipe featured within the book - prepared with Scottish porridge oats, full-fat milk, a pinch of salt and honey, sourced from her very own hives at her Wiltshire home.

Come summer, she switches to yoghurt. According to Parker Bowles, her lunches are modest as well; frequently the chicken broth - another recipe featured in the book - or smoked salmon, while Charles famously skips lunch entirely, but has dried fruit and honey for breakfast, and is particularly fond of mutton.

Previously extracted from Cooking And The Crown by Tom Parker Bowles, published in hardback by Aster

News.title: Keir Starmer's united front with Angela Rayner and Andy Burnham ahead of crunch elections
News.content:
Keir Starmer's united front with Angela Rayner and Andy Burnham ahead of crunch elections

The Prime Minister - who faces dire predictions Labour could lose up to 2,000 councillors - insisted the party would 'take nothing for granted' in May's local elections

View Image Keir Starmer with Angela Rayner and Andy Burnham during a visit to Greater Manchester on Monday (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News)

Keir Starmer attempted to present a united front with Angela Rayner and Andy Burnham today - ahead of next month's crunch local elections.

‌



The Prime Minister - who faces dire predictions Labour could lose up to 2,000 councillors - insisted the party would "take nothing for granted" in May's poll.

‌



He also dismissed the possibility that he could resign if Labour suffered heavy defeats, telling reporters he had received a “five-year mandate to change this country” in 2024. He added: “I intend to carry through that mandate.”

‌



Mr Starmer was joined on the visit by his former deputy, Ms Rayner, and Greater Manchester Mayor Mr Burnham, whose bid to contest the Gorton and Denton by-election was blocked by Labour’s ruling executive committee.

While the trio appeared united - sharing a joke as they sat with schoolchildren - Ms Rayner has become increasingly vocal in her criticism of the Government in recent weeks.

‌



Why Anas Sarwar thinks 'underdogs' Labour can win Scottish elections READ MORE :

The former Deputy Prime Minister, who is often floated as a potential future leadership candidate, warned last month Labour was "running out of time" to deliver change.

Addressing an event by campaign group Mainstream, Ms Ryaner said the party had come to be seen to represent "the Establishment, not working people".

She also hit out at the government's flagship immigration plans spearheaded by the Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood. In an apparent attack on the proposals, Ms Rayner said: "Many people came here to Britain - on the understanding that if they worked in the sectors where we needed them, obeyed the law and paid their taxes, they could stay.

Article continues below

"If we suddenly change that, it pulls the rug from under those who have planned their lives and commitments and are contributing to our economy and to our society. That would be not just bad policy but a breach of trust. The people already in the system - who made a huge investment - now fear for their future, they do not have stability and do not know what will happen.

"We cannot talk about earning a settlement if we keep moving the goalposts, because moving the goalposts undermines our sense of fair play. It's un-British."

She continued: "As a party, and as a movement, we cannot hide, we cannot just go through the motions in the face of decline. There's no safe ground and we're running out of time. The change that people wanted so desperately needs to be seen, it needs to be felt, and we have to show that it is a Labour government that will deliver it."

News.title: Dr Meghan Rossi explains 'common issue' which stops people eating enough fibre
News.content:
Dr Meghan Rossi explains 'common issue' which stops people eating enough fibre

Dr Meghan Rossi said it was not simply a case of eating more plants

View 2 Images Dr Rossi says you need to think about 'fibre efficiency' if you want to hit your goals (stock image)

A doctor renowned for her expertise in gut health has revealed that getting enough fibre each day is not simply a matter of 'eating more plants'. Dr Meghan Rossi, widely known as the Gut Health Doctor, has built a reputation for her knowledge in health and nutrition.

‌



On Instagram, where she boasts nearly 600,000 followers, she addressed the issue of fibre consumption. Current figures reveal that more than 90 per cent of Britons fall short of their daily fibre requirements.

‌



More concerningly, just 7 per cent of Brits are aware that the target is 30g of fibre daily, with most believing the figure sits around 12.4g. Back in 2015, the UK Government increased its recommended fibre intake guidelines from 24g to 30g.

‌



The typical Brit consumes merely 16g of fibre per day, with only 4 per cent meeting the daily target. Adequate fibre consumption is linked to reduced risks of heart disease, stroke, type 2 diabetes and bowel cancer.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

You would be forgiven for assuming that simply increasing your daily fruit and vegetable intake would address the issue - but Dr Rossi insists more consideration is required. She said: "It's not just about eating more plants.

‌



"Different plants pack very different amounts of fibre. If you're aiming for that 30g a day, focusing on more "fibre-efficient" foods can make hitting that target a lot easier."

She shared a series of graphs exploring 'fibre efficiency', demonstrating exactly how much of particular foods you'd need to consume simply to reach 5g of fibre. To illustrate, you'd need to consume nearly a kilogramme of cucumbers simply to obtain 5g of fibre, while the same quantity can be reached with merely 625g of melon, 47g of porridge oats, and only 14g of chia seeds.

Looking at vegetables particularly, 5g of fibre can be sourced from 417g of peppers, 192g of broccoli, and 131g of Brussels sprouts. Regarding wholegrains, 5g of fibre is present in 147g of brown rice, 50g of wholewheat pasta, and 32g of pearl barley.

‌



Bananas provide 5g of fibre per 294g of fruit, with blueberries delivering the same quantity of fibre in only 208g. Superfood favourite avocado takes the lead, offering 5g of fibre in merely 75g of fruit.

Turning to legumes, tofu contains 5g of fibre per 263g, while you require just 111g of frozen peas for the equivalent amount. Kidney beans provide 5g of fibre per 91g, while lentils deliver the same quantity of fibre in just one 63g portion.

Lastly, nuts - a nutritional powerhouse - are excellent sources of fibre. Pistachios contain 5g of fibre per 53g, while almonds have the same amount in only 40g. As previously mentioned, chia seeds top the list with 5g of fibre per merely 14g of seeds.

‌



"In clinic, a common issue I see is people eating more plants, but still falling short of their 30g of fibre. I'm a gut scientist and dietitian, and there is one concept I see people miss all the time," Dr Rossi explained. "Fibre efficiency. It's simple: how much of a food do you actually need to eat to get a meaningful amount of fibre? You need much smaller portions of some foods to get 5g of fibre, whereas you need much greater volumes of other foods to get the same amount of fibre.

"And this is where people get stuck. Yes, plant diversity matters, because different gut microbes need different plants to thrive. But if most of your choices are low efficiency on fibre, you may still struggle to hit your 30g of fibre."

View 2 Images Simply eating more plants may not be the best way to up your fibre levels

‌



What exactly is fibre, and why is it important?

GutsUK explains: "In simple terms, fibre is a part of plant foods, such as fruits, vegetables, grains, pulses and seeds. It is something that your body simply can't digest. While other nutrients are absorbed in the small intestine, fibre travels all the way to your large bowel (colon).

"You could think of fibre as the ultimate multitasker for your gut. Some types of fibre add bulk to your poo and keep things moving smoothly to prevent constipation. Others act as a prebiotic, providing a feast for your gut bacteria. In return, these bacteria "pay rent" by producing essential nutrients that help to keep your gut healthy. Whether it's soluble, insoluble or resistant starch, fibre is vital for our health." Your large bowel houses trillions of microbes, referred to as your gut microbiome. Numerous bacteria are selective feeders that flourish on particular varieties of fibre. While they find the tougher, insoluble types challenging, they're drawn to soluble fibres (such as those present in oats).

When these fibres reach the bowel, your bacteria get to work fermenting them. In exchange for this meal, as we mentioned above, our bacteria “pay rent” by producing:

Article continues below

Short-chain fatty acids: Small fat molecules that nourish the cells lining your bowel.

Essential vitamins: Helping your body function from the inside out.For every extra 7g of fibre you add to your daily diet (which is the same as around two slices of wholemeal bread), you significantly reduce your risk of chronic disease:

8% reduction in colon cancer risk.

9% reduction in cardiovascular disease.

7% reduction in strokes.

By consuming lots of fibre, you boost beneficial bacteria such as Lactobacillus and Bifidobacteria, which bolster your immune system and general wellbeing. Put simply, a healthy fibre intake helps you sustain a healthier weight, reduced blood pressure and quite literally can contribute to a longer life.

News.title: 'My son was launched 10ft in air by balaclava-clad e-bike yobs - we need a ban'
News.content:
'My son was launched 10ft in air by balaclava-clad e-bike yobs - we need a ban'

A petition to ban balaclavas in the UK has now attracted over 50,000 signatures as one mum told how her eight-year-old son was left 'traumatised' after yobs with their faces covered ploughed into him

View 6 Images Ethan Hodson-Ridgway was rushed to hospital after being run over by an e-bike rider wearing a balaclava (Image: Amy Ridgway / SWNS)

A devastated mum has joined growing calls for Britain to ban balaclavas after her eight-year-old son was left 'traumatised' by masked thugs on E-bikes who ran him over. Ethan Hodson-Ridgway was launched 10ft into the air after two balaclava-clad yobs on an electric bike ploughed into him just outside his home in Manchester on December 20 last year. He suffered a broken tibia and fibula in his left leg, a collapsed lung and sustained a gash to his head, leaving him in hospital for a week over Christmas.

‌



His mum, Amy Hodson-Ridgway, 34, has since been campaigning for a ban on balaclavas - claiming they "provide anonymity to countless individuals committing crimes" - and is backing greater regulation on mopeds and e-bikes.

‌



View 6 Images The crash broke the tibia and fibula in Ethan's left leg (Image: Amy Ridgway / SWNS)

‌



Primrose Hill victim's friend heard harrowing screams on phone before student stabbed READ MORE :

The Change.org petition, which already has nearly 50,000 signatures, says that balaclavas and bikes without number plates “embolden criminals” and help them “evade accountability”.

Despite being footage being provided, Amy said police told her they were unable to identify the suspects who fled the scene due to their identities being hidden, leading to the case being closed just three weeks later.

Amy, from Denton, Manchester, who has since had to leave her job to take care of Ethan, said: "Balaclavas have provided anonymity to countless individuals committing crimes in our neighbourhood.

‌



"It has made it nearly impossible for law enforcement to identify and prosecute perpetrators.

"This single piece of clothing has turned our community into a breeding ground for lawlessness and fear.

"They embolden criminals, from petty thieves to dangerous drivers, allowing them to evade accountability."

‌



View 6 Images He also suffered a collapsed lung and a gash to his head (Image: Amy Ridgway / SWNS)

There are currently no laws outlawing the wearing of balaclavas, though local councils can use Public Space Protection Orders (PSPOs) to allow police to issue fines to those who refuse to remove face coverings. Police also have powers to ask people to remove face coverings at protests, and building owners can ask people to leave their premises if wearing them on private land.

Ethan had been with his stepfather, Charlie, 27, and twin sister Olivia as they made their way back from a day of "being spoiled" at the shops on the first day of their Christmas holidays.

‌



But while crossing the road he was hit by the two e-bike riders, who were travelling at around 45mph. Olivia frantically ran home to alert her mum. Amy explained: “It’s definitely traumatised us all – his twin sister, older brother Jack, Charlie and me.

“It was around six o’clock on the 20th, and they were crossing the road when out of nowhere this bike came out of nowhere at great speed, no lights, no plates, nothing, and hit Ethan head-on.

View 6 Images Ethan was 'traumatised' after being hospitalised only days before Christmas (Image: Amy Ridgway / SWNS)

‌



“I still have flashbacks of when his sister ran in the house to get me, the look of pure terror on her face. I ran outside, and luckily, they were right next to our house.

“I was expecting to see he’d just fallen, but he was on the floor, not even crying, but moaning, blood everywhere.

"I initially thought both legs were broken because one was so swollen, and you could see the bone under the skin of the other.

‌



“It was freezing, but I just sat on the concrete with him in my arms; it was horrible, he just kept saying to me ‘Is this real life mummy?’, he wasn’t with it, just awful.“

Ethan required stitches in his head at Royal Manchester Children's Hospital and had to wait to get a metal rod inserted into his leg as a result of the collapsed lung.

View 6 Images The aftermath of the crash has left other members of the family suffering 'flashbacks' (Image: Amy Ridgway / SWNS)

‌



The football and kickboxing-mad youngster still hasn't been able to return to the sports he loves, and the mum explained that the incident has affected other members of the family too.

She said: “Olivia was having severe flashbacks, wasn’t sleeping, getting really upset, and that was really hard. She only really settled when Ethan returned to school, but they’re still very hyper-aware and clingy when they hear bikes.

“This is a family populated area, but the bikes are going around everywhere, and the balaclavas are purely being used to hide someone’s identity so they can get away with things.

‌



“It was disappointing that the police didn’t do anything, but it’s also understandable; it’s hard to identify someone with one on. Only two or three days after Christmas, the bikes were back around the area, and I sent some footage to the police, but they didn’t take it.

"It’s impossible to identify them, the balaclavas are obviously the issue, and the bikes are really dangerous. They’re happy children, and Ethan’s resilience has pulled us all through it.

View 6 Images The boy's mum says the amount of support from the public has been 'heartwarming' (Image: Amy Ridgway / SWNS)

‌



“But when they’re out now, they’re always on high alert. On the walk to school, they’ll hear a bike and squeeze my hands, looking around. They don’t want to play out the front anymore, because our house goes onto a walkway and bikes are always flying past."

She said the recent Gorton and Denton by-election had prevented her raising the campaign on an official level, but she is now awaiting the next steps after getting in contact with her new MP.

For now, she hopes the petition will help bring to wider attention the issues present in her community for years - and is grateful for all the support she has received from the public.

Article continues below

She added: “I feel a lot of anger that Ethan was hurt, and these people got away with it, but the sense of community and love for Ethan has been heartwarming."

News.title: 'World's shortest IQ test' says a lot with three questions and just 17% pass it
News.content:
'World's shortest IQ test' says a lot with three questions and just 17% pass it

MIT professor Shane Frederick's Cognitive Reflection Test is a three-question brain teaser with only a 17 per cent pass rate - can you beat the odds and solve all three?

View 2 Images An IQ test is a great way to measure your knowledge (Image: seksan Mongkhonkhamsao via Getty Images)

IQ tests are a useful and straightforward method of measuring your intelligence.

‌



Typically, these assessments can be rather lengthy, running for over an hour with a wide range of questions designed to push your mind to its absolute limits. Despite this, many bright sparks may be astonished to discover that there exists an IQ test comprising just three questions.

‌



Yet, the brevity of the test doesn't make it any easier to crack. In fact, research revealed that a mere 17% of participants managed to pass the brainteaser.

‌



Known as the Cognitive Reflection Test, the quiz originally featured in a research paper published in 2005 by MIT professor Shane Frederick. Since resurfacing on the internet, the paper has gone viral as people scramble to find out whether they can conquer the "world's shortest IQ test".

As part of the study, Professor Frederick had more than 3,000 participants from a variety of educational backgrounds complete the IQ test. Of that sizeable group, only 17% succeeded in scoring three out of three.

Speaking about the test, Professor Frederick, said: "The three items on the CRT are 'easy' in the sense that their solution is easily understood when explained, yet reaching the correct answer often requires the suppression of an erroneous answer that springs 'impulsively' to mind".

‌



What are the questions?

View 2 Images Only 17 per cent of participants managed to pass this brain teaser (Image: Kohei Hara via Getty Images)

1. A bat and a ball cost $1.10 in total. The bat costs $1 more than the ball. How much does the ball cost?

2. If it takes five machines five minutes to make five widgets, how long would it take 100 machines to make 100 widgets?

‌



3. In a lake, there is a patch of lily pads. Every day, the patch doubles in size. If it takes 48 days for the patch to cover the entire lake, how long would it take for the patch to cover half of the lake?

Below you will find the three most common answers which are in fact all incorrect:

1. 10 cents

‌



2. 100 minutes

3. 24 days

Professor Frederick adds: "Anyone who reflects upon it for even a moment would recognise that the difference between $1 and 10 cents is only 90 cents, not $1 as the problem stipulates.

‌



"In this case, catching that error is tantamount to solving the problem, since nearly everyone who does not respond '10 cents' does, in fact, give the correct response."

What are the correct answers?

Read below to find the correct answers for each question:

1. 5 cents

‌



2. 5 minutes

3. 47 days

Still scratching your head even after seeing the solutions?

Article continues below

Presh Talwalkar, author of The Joy of Game Theory: An Introduction to Strategic Thinking, has stepped in to break down the reasoning behind each correct answer with the following explanations: 1. Say the ball costs X. Then the bat costs $1 more, so it is X + 1. So we have bat + ball = X + (X + 1) = 1.1 because together they cost $1.10. This means 2X + 1 = 1.1, then 2X = 0.1, so X = 0.05. This means the ball costs 5 cents and the bat costs $1.05

2. If it takes 5 machines 5 minutes to make 5 widgets, then it takes 1 machine 5 minutes to make 1 widget (each machine is making a widget in 5 minutes). If we have 100 machines working together, then each can make a widget in 5 minutes. So there will be 100 widgets in 5 minutes.

3. Every day FORWARD the patch doubles in size. So every day BACKWARDS means the patch halves in size. So on day 47 the lake is half full.

News.title: Mum who made thousands flogging fake Oasis tickets forced to pay victims back
News.content:
Mum who made thousands flogging fake Oasis tickets forced to pay victims back

Rosie Slater of Betley, Newcastle-under-Lyme, scammed fans out of around £4,000 by flogging fake VIP executive box seats for Wembley gigs of the Oasis reunion tour

View 2 Images Rosie Slater has been sentenced for flogging fake Oasis tickets (Image: StokeSentinel)

A mum who swindled thousands of pounds by flogging fake Oasis reunion tour tickets has been sentenced.

‌



Rosie Slater of Betley, Newcastle-under-Lyme, scammed fans by claiming to sell VIP executive box seats for the Wembley gigs. She made £4,000 in ill-gotten gains after tricking victims into parting with their money throughout May 2025.

‌



The mum-of-three raked in between £130-£160 for each ticket after putting them up for sale via chat groups.

‌



She pleaded guilty to 11 counts of fraud by false representation when she appeared at North Staffordshire Justice Centre last December. The charges relate to her pretending she had access to Oasis concert tickets and a VIP box at Wembley Stadium in May 2025, stated Staffordshire Police.

View 2 Images Slater made around £4,000 by flogging fake tickets (Image: Stoke Sentinel)

Slater was bailed ahead of a sentencing hearing today which took place at North Staffordshire Justice Centre.

‌



She was sentenced to a 12-month community order, requiring her to complete a mental health treatment requirement alongside 30 rehabilitation days. Slater was ordered to pay a £40 fine, a £114 victim surcharge and £85 in costs. She must fully compensate the victims to the amount of £776.98, bringing her total costs to £1015.98. It is understood that some victims have been paid back, reports StokeonTrentLive.

Magistrates said: “Ms Slater, you will be aware that we were outside for quite some time. We have assessed this case in quite some detail. You say this spiralled out of your control, which we acknowledge, but your actions cause loss and upset to many people.”

Her lawyer Simon Leach said: “She said she started with good intentions but the situation soon spiralled out of her control. She said she used the money to pay off her debts.” He added: "She has not spent this money extravagantly. She spent this money on common household bills such as council tax.”

Article continues below

The court previously heard she offered the tickets for the band's shows in August via WhatsApp because "she wanted to be popular". However Slater was rumbled when suspicious customers reported her to police and she was charged with multiple fraud offences.

Speaking following her conviction last December, DC David Stubbs of Staffordshire Police's investigation bureau, who investigated the case, said: “This was a complex case that involved multiple victims and a significant amount of money lost.

"Slater kept up the pretence enticing more victims and making personal gain whilst causing a financial loss to the victims." DC Stubbs also thanked the members of the public who came forward to alert us to this scam and provided key evidence for the investigation.

News.title: Ex-Arsenal star Thomas Partey pleads not guilty to two new allegations of rape
News.content:
Ex-Arsenal star Thomas Partey pleads not guilty to two new allegations of rape

Thomas Partey, the Ghana midfielder who spent five years at Arsenal, appeared at Southwark Crown Court on Monday over two allegations of rape

View 3 Images Thomas Partey has pleaded not guilty to two new rape allegations (Image: CARLOS JASSO/AFP via Getty Images)

Former Arsenal footballer Thomas Partey has pleaded not guilty to two new allegations of rape.

‌



The 32-year-old midfielder appeared at Southwark Crown Court on Monday to deny twice raping a woman in London on a day in December 2020.

‌



The star, who left Arsenal for Villarreal last summer, was charged in July last year with five counts of rape and one allegation of sexual assault, dating back to 2021 and 2022.

‌



He previously pleaded not guilty to those charges, and a trial was set for November this year.

View 3 Images Partey appeared at Southwark Crown Court on Monday

The two new rape charges were announced in February this year, and on Monday Judge Tony Baumgartner, the Recorder of Westminster, agreed for all the allegations to be tried together.

‌



But he warned Partey and lawyers in the case that the trial could now be delayed until January next year.

In total, the footballer has now pleaded not guilty to seven counts of rape and one count of sexual assault, relating to allegations from four different women.

Partey, wearing dark grey trousers, a black jumper over a white shirt, and smart black shoes, spoke to confirm his name and enter the two not guilty pleas during Monday’s hearing.

‌



He left the dock with his charcoal grey suit jacket slung over his left shoulder.

Partey was absent from Westminster Magistrates’ Court last month when the charges came before a judge for the first time.

View 3 Images Partey pictured outside court

‌



But his lawyer indicated that not guilty pleas would be entered.

The Ghanaian midfielder, who previously lived in Potters Bar in Hertfordshire, joined Arsenal from Atletico Madrid in 2020 in a transfer worth around £45 million, before he left the club in June last year.

He is expected to face England in the World Cup this summer, as an integral part of the Ghana national side.

‌



Partey is on bail during the legal proceedings, with a condition that he does not contact alleged victims.

The court heard Mr Justice Bennathan is expected to be the trial judge.

Partey’s case is next due to be listed in court, for a pre-trial hearing, on May 14.

Article continues below

A decision will be taken on the exact trial date when the judge has been confirmed.

News.title: Fed-up woman 'feels like concierge' as neighbour diverts all parcels her way
News.content:
Fed-up woman 'feels like concierge' as neighbour diverts all parcels her way

A frustrated resident shared how she has been taking in all of her neighbour's parcels daily – but she's growing tired of being their personal concierge service

View 2 Images One woman said she feels like her neighbours are using her as a makeshift "concierge service" (Image: Jackyenjoyphotography via Getty Images)

As everyone knows, neighbourly relations can either be harmonious and respectful or somewhat strained and uncomfortable.

‌



And unfortunately, this frustrated resident has fallen into the second category. The homeowner revealed they've just relocated to a new property in a cul de sac, alongside four other homes.

‌



One of their neighbours has a "scary-looking gate" which is electric and has its own intercom system. But despite the beefy security system, they don't have a working doorbell.

‌



This has led to plenty of parcels being delivered to the fed-up people next door – and the selfish neighbours don't even seem concerned about inconveniencing others.

At her wit's end, the anonymous woman took to Mumsnet to ask for advice about how to handle the uncomfortable situation.

View 2 Images The neighbour's doorbell is faulty meaning they never get notifications for their deliveries (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The post reads: "Am I being unreasonable to not want to be concierge service for new neighbours.

"Very soon after moving in - having had brief but very friendly interactions with the neighbours - it became clear that the intercom/doorbell for the gate was not working properly.

"There is a barrage of deliveries from DPD, Hermes, Royal Mail etc. Delivery men asked if we would take them, we agreed assuming that the doorbell was not temporarily working properly.

‌



"Bear in mind that in virtually all cases I believe they were in, but no way to let them know other than shouting or jumping over a high wall (not realistic as there is a spikey hedge on the other side).

"Next time I saw them I shouted over the wall and mentioned that I had parcels, they came to collect and I made a joke about the bell not working. I expected a 'yeah sorry we're on with that' but actually got words to the effect of 'no it hasn't worked for years and we don't intend to get it fixed'. I was so gobsmacked I didn't know what to say."

While the resident doesn't mind occasionally accepting deliveries for a neighbour, it's now become a "daily occurrence" and the favour is rarely repaid.

‌



So, she asked: "Am I being unreasonable to not want to take in all the parcels? And if I'm not being unreasonable how do I approach this with them, bearing in mind we really want to foster friendly relations with all neighbours."

Thankfully, people were quick to offer their advice. They proposed a simple solution – refusing to take the parcels in until their neighbours got the message to fix the doorbell.

One commenter advised: "I just would refuse to take in the parcels. You don't need to speak to them just don't accept them. Not your problem."

Article continues below

Another said: "Just stop taking them. This is a problem for them, not you. They won't get it fixed because they know you'll do it. Once they start not getting deliveries, they'll get it fixed."

And a third added: "I don’t think it’s passive aggressive to simply stop taking parcels for them."

News.title: Where does McIlroy rank among golf's greats after Masters defence?
News.content:
A surefire sign of a sports star who wants to achieve true greatness is the ability to recalibrate, realign and reach their next goal.

Jack Nicklaus had that quality. Tiger Woods also had it.

Rory McIlroy is highly unlikely to reach the same number of major wins as the two finest golfers to have ever picked up a club but, after becoming only the fourth player to successfully defend the Masters title, he has shown he has the same ability to chase down new targets.

Last year at Augusta National, McIlroy also earned his place in history as the sixth man to sweep the board at the four major tournaments - the Masters, US PGA Championship, the Open Championship and the US Open.

Afterwards, he searched for new purpose having scaled his "golfing Everest".

It is no secret of where his ambitions lie now: climbing as high as possible on the list of major wins.

"If you win more than one major you're semi-elite. To have won three of the majors means you have had an exceptional career," Ken Brown, the BBC golf commentator and former European Ryder Cup player said.

"But to win the Grand Slam and back-to-back Masters? It puts you in the spot where you are living with the absolute greats who have played the game in the modern era."

After securing a sixth major title at Augusta National on Sunday, where does the 36-year-old from Northern Ireland go next and where does he now sit in the pantheon of golfing greats?

News.title: McIlroy underlines greatness by defending Masters title
News.content:
Rory McIlroy underlined why he is one of the game's greats by holding off the world's best to become only the fourth man to win successive Masters titles.

McIlroy's belief that finally landing the Green Jacket last year would pave the way for more major victories proved prophetic.

Twelve months ago, the 36-year-old from Northern Ireland ended an 11-year wait to complete the career Grand Slam by winning at Augusta National, a victory which he felt would allow him to play with more freedom when he returned in the future.

That is exactly what he has been able to do - at the first opportunity.

McIlroy shot a final-day 71 to finish on 12 under, one stroke clear of world number one Scottie Scheffler, on another Masters Sunday for the ages.

"I can't believe I waited 17 years to get one Green Jacket and now I get two in a row," said McIlroy, who clinched his sixth major to draw level with England's Sir Nick Faldo.

"All my perseverance at this golf course over the years has started to pay off."

News.content:

Booker Prize-winning author David Szalay has found himself at the centre of speculation about authorial inspiration and homage, as readers of his novel Flesh have questioned whether a film by Stanley Kubrick inspired the book almost “beat for beat”.

The sixth novel by Canadian-Hungarian writer Szalay, Flesh was released in March 2025. It follows a young working-class man called István, who over the course of his life rises up the ranks from poverty at home in Hungary to sitting among London’s elite.

The book, which became a talking point for its sparse prose and 500 repeats of the word “OK”, won the 2025 Booker Prize; at the time, awards chair Roddy Doyle said that the judges had “never read anything quite like it”.

However, a number of critics and readers have noted similarities between Szalay’s book and Kubrick’s 1975 film Barry Lyndon, which itself is adapted from William Makepeace Thackeray’s 1844 novel The Luck of Barry Lyndon.

Barry Lyndon’s eponymous lead comes from Ireland, not Hungary, yet the characters follow near identical trajectories: they enlist in the army, marry wealthy women, grieve their sons and clash with their stepsons, and lose everything they have earned later in their lives.

But despite the similarities in the plots, Szalay has not listed Kubrick’s film as an inspiration for the story or writing process. This has led to some readers speculating that Szalay is playing an elaborate game and has included Easter eggs referencing Barry Lyndon in his novel.

open image in gallery Szalay with Queen Camilla at the Booker Prize reception last year ( PA )

In Kubrick’s film, Barry is shown a painting and comments: “I love the use of the colour blue by the artist.” In Flesh, Istvan is taken to the National Gallery and says of a different painting: "I like the use of the colour blue in that one.”

The Independent has contacted Szalay’s representatives for comment.

What critics said at the time

Flesh received rave reviews upon its release, with few critics at the time noting the similarities between Barry Lyndon and Flesh.

The first reference appears to have been made by Aled Maclean-Jones in June 2025 on the Substack publication The Republic of Letters, where he suggests that Flesh is “quite clearly, a near beat-for-beat mirror – both of the novel and of Kubrick’s film adaptation, to such a level I’d almost call it a retelling”.

In July, The New Statesman published a cultural reexamination of Barry Lyndon, where writer David Sexton argued that the similarities between Flesh and Kubrick’s film was a sign of the story’s “continued potency”.

“Unnoticed by most reviewers and uncommented upon by Szalay himself, Flesh – which is about the picaresque career of its hero István, from Hungary to London, from poverty to riches and back to poverty again – is nothing less than a thorough revision and updating of Barry Lyndon (Kubrick’s movie, not Thackeray’s novel),” he wrote.

open image in gallery Szalay will deny that 'Flesh' was written as a homage to 'Barry Lyndon' in a new interview ( AFP/Getty )

Sexton doubled down on his argument in The Standard following Szalay’s Booker Prize win, where he put forward that Flesh was Barry Lyndon “updated, relocated, re-imagined, but the same”.

“There is nothing remotely wrong about it. It’s not plagiarism. Indeed, it could be considered a vital tribute to a fantastic film,” he wrote.

What Szalay has said

What makes the whole debacle quite so strange is that Szalay has shared his influences for Flesh, but Kubrick’s film hasn’t been one of them.

Appearing on Dua Lipa’s Service95 Book Club podcast, the author listed Hamlet, Virginia Woolf’s Jacob’s Room, Joseph Conrad’s Lord Jim, Michel Houellebecq’s Platform and Katherine Faw’s Ultra Luminous as the five books that had influenced Flesh, with no reference to either Kubrick’s film or Thackeray’s novel.

In an interview with The Observer from November, Lyndon said that he had seen Barry Lyndon when he was 20, and said that “the rags-to-riches arc was an influence”.

Szalay is explicitly asked about the similarities between the texts in a forthcoming episode of BBC Radio 4’s This Cultural Life, where he’s asked if Flesh is a “direct reference” to Barry Lyndon.

“No, I wouldn’t go that far,” Szalay replies, adding that Kubrick’s film “wasn’t really at the front of my mind, I don’t think”. When pressed, he says that he could have been “influenced by it in some way”, but denies that his book was written in homage to the film.

Fresh fuel protests caused traffic disruption across Ireland's motorways on Monday, despite the government's half-a-billion-euro package to address rising costs.

While blockades at fuel depots and Ireland’s only oil refinery were lifted, smaller protests continued on motorways near Dublin. A Facebook page, a source of protest information, posted conflicting messages on Sunday night, suggesting both continued action on Monday and that "all protestors and Gardai go home".

Slow-moving convoys of large vehicles on Monday morning caused delays on motorways including the M50 southbound, the M1 southbound in Co Louth, and the M9 at Athy, Co Kildare.

A spokesman for the Dublin fuel protest said the protesters “achieved something small” in 505 million euros worth of government measures announced on Sunday, but that he has “no control” over further protests.

Protesters – largely led by hauliers, farmers, and agricultural workers – began distinct but co-ordinated action on Tuesday with slow-moving convoys and outright stoppages on major motorways, as well as blockades of critical infrastructure which had largely wound down or been disbanded by police by midday on Sunday.

A package was announced on Sunday evening for fuel-dependent workers affected by rising fuel costs triggered by the US and Israeli war in Iran and the effective shutdown by Iran of the Strait of Hormuz.

open image in gallery Protesters make their way to O'Connell Street on Saturday during the National Fuel Protest, in Dublin, Ireland. ( Copyright 2026 The Associated Press. All rights reserved. )

It was worth around 505 million euros, and comes on top of 250 million euros worth of measures announced almost three weeks ago.

Social Protection Minister Dara Calleary said the protesters had not won as engagement had been ongoing with farming and transport representative groups on further support before the protests began on Tuesday.

He told Raidio na Gaeltachta that the two packages announced by the Irish government were among the largest in Europe, and that the measures would have an influence on the government’s budget in October.

The seventh day of disruption on Monday comes as the government faces a motion of no confidence in the Irish parliament on Tuesday.

The main opposition party Sinn Fein is to table the motion criticising the government for not reconvening the Dail last week and not engaging directly with the protesters, while also calling on the government to take the “maximum action necessary” to cut fuel prices.

Sinn Fein finance spokesman Pearse Doherty criticised the government for “laughable” measures announced on Sunday, the government’s second response to fuel price rises caused by the US and Israeli war in Iran.

“Again, they come up short, and that’s why so many people are annoyed this morning,” Mr Doherty said on Monday.

“Nobody wanted to be out there. The government forced people to take the street.

open image in gallery Sinn Fein’s Pearse Doherty criticised the government for “laughable” measures announced on Sunday. ( PA Wire )

“Indeed, the government made matters worse. They went from insulting people, to demeaning them, to threaten them with the army, to refuse to talk to people and try and resolve this.”

He added: “For many people, yes, it was about fuel.

“Yes, it was about petrol, diesel, home heating oil, but it was also about all of the other pressures that people are feeling – whether it’s energy costs, whether it’s groceries, whether it’s rents that continue to go up, and basically a tipping point that the government aren’t listening, that we needed something to happen in terms of (a) cost (of) living package.”

A spokesman for the protesters said they had no control over the more regional demonstrations.

“Nobody knows what the plan is, that’s being straight out there,” said John Dallon, a Kildare farmer and agriculture contractor who was at the Dublin protest.

He said he welcomed the measures on green diesel, but the government “should have done something” on kerosene.

“This protest is out of my hands, it escalated to somewhat so big, and I don’t know where it’s going to end, but it’s the government’s fault,” he told Newstalk radio on Monday.

“We achieved something small, but this is something way bigger now, and I have no control over it, and that’s exactly where I’m coming from.

“It’s gone to the stage that it seems like, looking out there, that the people of the island of Ireland have no confidence in this government anymore.”

The Philippine President did a few rounds of star jumps before jogging briefly outside his office in front of journalists in a bid to disprove rumours of his failing health.

Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said he did the impromptu workout to ease any worry about his health at a time when people were already beset with problems sparked by the war in the Middle East.

The 68-year-old leader was wearing formal office wear, reading glasses and leather shoes.

“I challenge anyone who are saying that I am sick, that they come and exercise with me,” Marcos told reporters. “You come to the gym with me. Let’s see who can lift the weights better.”

“Those people who tell you that I’m sick, that I’m paralysed, they’re all liars,” Marcos said.

Rumours about the president’s deteriorating health and even death have swirled on social media after he briefly vanished from public view in January, then later acknowledged in a video message that he was taken to a hospital for an abdominal ailment that he ascribed to stress and age.

Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. ( AP )

Marcos then laughed off rumours of his demise and said he had been diagnosed with diverticulitis. The condition involves inflammation of small pouches in the digestive tract, usually in the colon, that causes pain, fever, nausea or constipation.

His last hospital checkup a couple of months ago showed he had been cured of that ailment, Marcos said, and added that he was back on a normal diet and was regularly exercising.

When asked if he was taking any maintenance medicine, Marcos said he was taking medication for gout and for high blood pressure.

Since taking office in mid-2022, Marcos has grappled with multiple complex problems and political dilemmas.

Those include an increasingly hostile territorial dispute with Beijing in the South China Sea, devastating earthquakes, typhoons and flooding, economic difficulties, tumultuous relations with his vice president and a corruption scandal involving powerful legislators and allies that has sparked public outrage.
